title: Trials and free tiers
standfirst: “Free trial” covers four different offers: a time-limited trial that converts, a one-off credit, a free plan that never charges, and a recurring allowance. They differ in what you get and what happens on day eight.
idea: A time-limited trial gives access for a fixed number of days and then either charges you or stops. A one-off credit is money added to a prepaid balance once, spent at normal rates. A free plan is a permanent tier with hard caps. A recurring allowance is free usage that returns every month.

The card is not the dividing line. A trial with a card usually converts when its clock runs out. A credit with a card is spent and then stops. A free plan or allowance with no card never charges, but caps size and runtime instead. Read the ending as three questions: is the card charged, does a paid plan start, and does the allowance stop?

The unit matters too. Five dollars is about 100 hours of Agent 37's entry shape, and less than an hour of boxd's largest machine. Twenty-five hours at Boat is capped by a mandatory two-hour auto-stop, so it cannot test an always-on agent.

splits.heading: The one that converts itself
body: Sandboxer's seven-day trial becomes $20 a month on day eight. Boat's trial ends by charging the plan chosen at checkout. Lizard's trial ends and you either subscribe to Pro at $19 or stop creating things. Those are the three that end at a paid plan.
Everything else is spent, not converted: E2B's $100 credit, boxd's $30, Agent 37's $5, Blaxel's credits, Sprites' $1, Morph's disputed 300 hours, Runtime's allowance and InstaBox's free plan.

splits.heading: The free plans have hard caps
body: InstaBox's free plan gives one 4 vCPU / 8 GiB machine, two templates, and a fixed 30-minute idle pause. Runtime's free usage caps at 2 vCPU / 4 GiB / 10 GiB, four sandboxes at once and 50 created a day. Vercel's Hobby plan is non-commercial and pauses sandbox creation when its quotas run out.
Those caps are the product decision. A free plan that cannot stay up is not a substitute for a cheap paid one.

splits.heading: Credits run out silently
body: A credit is spent at the same rates as paid usage, so its value depends on the shape and the provider. When E2B's credit runs out without a payment method, every project in the workspace is blocked shortly afterwards. boxd's credit is drawn from a prepaid balance; there is no plan to fall back on.
A credit is not a trial: it does not expire on a date, it expires when the money does.

watchFor: Whether a card is required, and whether a paid plan starts automatically.
Whether the allowance is money, hours or a machine, and at which size.
Whether the free tier can stay up, or is capped by idle pause and session limits.
Whether a second trial is available on the same account or card.
What happens when a credit runs out: block, stop, or charge.

rows.scenario: A one-off $5 Cloud credit after adding a card, plus a $0 managed-hosting plan that now also needs a card on file; the credit is not granted to workspaces made through the signup API.
rows.note: A one-off $5 Cloud credit after adding a card, and a $0 managed-hosting plan with a card on file. The credit is not granted to workspaces created through the signup API. Before the first top-up a workspace can run 3 instances of any type, VMs included; more after top-ups (50 at $50, 1,000 at $1,000), counting awake instances only.

source.quote: Add a card from the billing page (nothing is charged) and your workspace gets a one-time $5 credit

rows.scenario: Up to $200 in promotional credits advertised; the actual grant, expiry and card requirement are not published.
rows.note: Up to $200 in promotional credits advertised on pay-as-you-go. The actual grant, expiry and card requirement are not published. Quota tiers are wallet top-ups, not fees.

source.quote: Up to $200 in free credits

rows.scenario: A seven-day trial with a card: 25 hours in total, two sandboxes, small and default sizes, and a mandatory two-hour auto-stop.
rows.note: A seven-day trial with a card and no free tier: 25 hours in total, two sandboxes at once, small and default sizes, a mandatory two-hour auto-stop and no new saved snapshots.

source.quote: 25 hours in total, all sandboxes together

rows.scenario: A one-off €30/$30 credit after adding a payment method; without one, an organisation is capped at two machines with no published allowance.
rows.note: A one-off €30/$30 credit after adding a payment method. No hosted free plan; an organisation without a payment method is capped at two machines. Self-hosting is free up to 16 worker vCPUs.

source.quote: €30 of credits when you add a payment method. Nothing is charged when you add the card

rows.scenario: There is no free sandbox: the $5 Workers Paid plan is required, and its included container usage is worth about $0.73.
rows.note: No free tier for containers; the Free column is N/A. Workers Paid has a $5 monthly minimum and includes 25 GiB-hours, 375 vCPU-minutes and 200 GB-hours of container usage.

source.quote: Available on Workers Paid plan

rows.scenario: The trial is $200 of compute with no card and no published expiry; GPU sandboxes cannot spend it.
rows.note: A $200 free compute credit with no card, and Tier 1 access by email verification. The credit is not available for GPU sandboxes; its expiry is not published.

source.quote: $200 in free compute included

rows.scenario: A one-time $100 credit with no card; when it runs out without a payment method, every project is blocked shortly afterwards.
rows.note: A one-time $100 usage credit on Hobby, with no card to start. When it runs out without a payment method, every project in the workspace is blocked shortly afterwards.

source.quote: One-time $100 in usage credits.

rows.scenario: A real free plan: one 4 vCPU / 8 GiB machine, 20 GiB disk, five snapshots, a fixed 30-minute idle pause and runs of at most 480 minutes, and it never converts.
rows.note: A real free plan: one 4 vCPU / 8 GiB machine, 20 GiB fixed disk, five snapshots, 100 GiB egress, a fixed 30-minute idle pause, at most 480 minutes per run and four templates. No GPU. It never converts.

source.quote: 1 machine, 4 vCPU / 8 GiB

rows.scenario: Seven days with $5 of usage, a card required, Small machines only and US regions only.
rows.note: A seven-day trial with $5 of usage and a card required. Until the first paid invoice an account runs 1 Small and 2 Mini at a time, in US regions only, and each sandbox is deleted an hour after it starts. One trial per account and per card.

source.quote: Pro starts with a 7-day trial that includes $5 of usage.

rows.scenario: Starter gives $30 of compute a month, but a payment method is required before anything runs.
rows.note: Starter is $0 plus compute with $30 a month of credits; Team is $250 plus compute with $100. A payment method is required to use Modal.

source.quote: $30 / month free credits

rows.scenario: Signup docs promise 300 free compute hours a month; the pricing page lists 0 MCUs and says to purchase them.
rows.note: Signup docs promise 300 free compute hours a month on the $0 Developer plan; the pricing page lists 0 MCUs and says to purchase MCUs. An invite is mentioned.

source.quote: Once you have your invite, our $0/month Developer Plan provides 300 free compute hours per month

rows.scenario: Recurring free usage with no card: 100 hours of a 1 GB machine with hard caps on size and concurrency.
rows.note: Recurring free usage with no card: 100 hours of a 1 GB machine, memory and CPU allowances, and hard caps on size and concurrency. Accounts that never pay get it once across 30 days.

source.quote: 100 free hours of a 1 GB machine

rows.scenario: No free tier and no trial: choosing a plan charges the first month immediately, and a card is needed before the first sandbox.
rows.note: No free tier or trial for new accounts since 2 November 2026; $20 a month is the floor. Signup, docs, CLI and dashboard need no card, but creating a sandbox needs a plan and a card. Trials started earlier keep their limits until they end.

source.quote: the first month is charged when you subscribe

rows.scenario: New accounts get $1 for 7 days with no card; after that, a personal org's bill under $5 is waived.
rows.note: $1 of credit for 7 days with no card, personal org only and at most 3 Sprites at a time. After that there is no free compute, but a personal org's monthly bill under $5 is waived and every org gets 20 GB of cold storage free each month.

source.quote: New accounts get $1 of free credit, with no credit card required.

rows.scenario: Hobby quotas restricted to non-commercial use, or a 14-day Pro trial with $20 in credits.
rows.note: Hobby has included quotas but is restricted to non-commercial use, and pauses sandbox creation when quotas run out. Pro has a 14-day trial with $20 in credits.

source.quote: The trial plan includes a $20 credit

rows.scenario: A free account runs one 1 vCPU / 1 GB sandbox for up to two hours at a time, with no card, and nothing converts on its own.
rows.note: Free is $0 forever with no credit card: 1 concurrent sandbox, 1 vCPU / 1 GB / 10 GB, 2-hour sessions, unmetered sessions and SOC 2. Usage Credits begin with a $5 pack you choose; unused credits are kept rather than refunded and come back if you return to the plan.

source.quote: You can start on our Free tier and run 1 sandbox at a time — no credit card required.

rows.scenario: A $5 credit for 90 days, but a payment method is required before the first Droplet exists.
rows.note: No free tier. A $5 signup credit expires after 90 days, and a card or PayPal must be on file before any Droplet can be created. Managed Agents has a separate $5 trial that the blog says needs no card; that is a different product.

source.quote: Signup credits expire 90 days after signup.

rows.scenario: The account needs a payment method before the first server, and the cheapest buyable plan today is CPX02 at €5.99 / $7.49 for the server plus €0.50 / $0.60 for an IPv4.
rows.note: No free tier, no automatic signup credit and no card-free trial: an account needs a card, SEPA direct debit, bank transfer or PayPal, invoices are due immediately, and new projects start with a small limit that is only raised after a month and a paid invoice. Promo codes exist but are handed out case by case. The advertised €5.99 Cost-Optimized plans are marked not available for ordering.

source.quote: We accept the following payment methods:

rows.scenario: A week of testing costs a month's plan; the 30-day money-back guarantee is the only way out.
rows.note: No ongoing free tier, no starting credit and no card-free trial. KVM VPS plans are refundable within 30 days, with a 180-day cooldown after a VPS refund.

source.quote: The Hostinger refund policy offers a 30-day money-back guarantee for most hosting and email services, such as web, cloud, and KVM VPS hosting plans.

rows.scenario: Try it: the Free plan runs a light workload inside 200 vCPU-hours, 400 GiB-hours and 60,000 GiB-hours a month, with no card.
rows.note: Free is a hard stop, not paid overage. The only published credit is a $5,000 deal for YC founders; there is no general signup credit.

source.quote: No credit card required.

rows.scenario: There is no free tier and no starting credit; you pay the first invoice before the server exists and can ask for the money back within 14 days.
rows.note: No free plan, no trial credit and no free sandbox hours. A card is not required — invoices can be paid by Bankgiro, Swish or SEPA as well as by card — but the server is created only once the invoice is paid. The safety net is a 14-day money-back guarantee on a new VPS order, two days if you are outside the EU/EEA.

source.quote: On a new order of VPS or web hosting, both Consumers and Business Customers have a money-back guarantee for 14 days from activation, or for two days if you live or have your registered office outside the EU/EEA when you order.

rows.scenario: A week of testing costs a full month: VPS-1 is $5.35 from the first invoice, there is no trial credit to burn, and a payment method is required before the order.
rows.note: No free tier and no published signup credit for VPS. A payment method (bank card, PayPal or SEPA direct debit) is required, the first invoice is the full month, and the service renews automatically until cancelled.

source.quote: To ensure that your services are renewed properly, you will need to set at least one payment method in the OVHcloud Control Panel.

rows.scenario: A new AWS account gets up to $200 of credits for six months; there is no recurring free Lightsail allowance after that.
rows.note: Lightsail's own short-term trials have been retired and replaced by AWS Free Tier credits: $100 at sign-up plus up to $100 earned, on an account that closes after six months or when the credits run out. A payment method is required to open the account.

source.quote: Lightsail’s short-term free trial offers have been replaced by the AWS Free Tier.

rows.figure: Free tier by application; deposit match
rows.scenario: A new account can apply for one small free instance in three regions, or use a promo code that matches a first deposit; a card is still needed for paid servers.
rows.note: The Free Tier Program offers 1 vCPU / 512 MB / 10 GB in Miami, Seattle and Frankfurt to eligible applicants, on a limited and randomized basis. Otherwise credit comes from promo codes or a dollar-for-dollar deposit match up to $100, not an automatic signup credit.

source.quote: Vultr is offering free cloud compute instances to eligible applicants!

rows.scenario: No free week and no starting credit: the first invoice is paid before the server exists.
rows.note: Contabo advertises no free tier, trial or signup credit on its pricing, VPS or order pages, and the cheapest 1-month plan is paid at order. Payment can be card, PayPal or bank transfer, but nothing runs before it clears.

source.quote: Provisioning takes a few minutes after payment clears.

rows.scenario: A week of testing is covered by the $100 credit, but a card is required at signup and the credit expires with the trial.
rows.note: A one-off promotional credit for new customers only, excluding GPU plans; unused credit expires and there is no ongoing free allowance. A valid payment method is required to open the account.

source.quote: Promotional credits are available only to new customers who have not yet signed up for a free trial.

rows.scenario: A new Business account with a card can start with €100 of credit, but there is no free Instance size and the card stays on the account afterwards.
rows.note: New Business customers with a valid payment method and no prior Scaleway invoice receive a €100 voucher by email within 24 hours, which must be redeemed. No ongoing free tier covers Instances, prepaid cards are refused, and a card is required even when SEPA is used.

source.quote: Create a Business account and get started with €100 free credit.

rows.scenario: Registration needs no card and grants a cent of credit, but the homepage says $3 must be added before the service can be used.
rows.note: A free account is created with a username and email, no card, and the price feed grants $0.01 of sign-up credit — about 74 hours on the smallest 128 MB server. The homepage also says a $3 minimum top-up is required to use the service, so whether that cent is spendable before you pay is unclear. There is no ongoing free VPS tier; the free static hosting is a separate product. A 14-day refund exists only if the service was barely used.

source.quote: A $3 minimum top up is required after registration to use this service.

rows.scenario: There is no free tier and no starting credit; you pay the first invoice before the server exists and can ask for the money back within seven days only if the fault is HostHatch's.
rows.note: No free plan, trial credit or free sandbox hours appear on the product page, the signup page or the terms. The only safety net is a 7-day money-back guarantee that requires a valid reason caused by HostHatch and evidence in a ticket; used resources may be deducted, and upgrades, setup fees and all non-VPS services are excluded. The payment methods accepted at signup are not published.

source.quote: Our virtual private servers (VPS) carry a 7-day money back guarantee with a valid reason requirement.

figureLabel: What you get, and what ends it

scenario.title: A week of testing, then a small agent that stays up
scenario.setup: You want seven days to test, then one small always-available agent. The trial has to answer three questions: is a card needed, does a paid plan start by itself, and can the free machine stay up?

beats.what: You sign up. A card may be required before the first machine exists.
The trial ends. It either converts to a paid plan, stops, or keeps spending a credit.
The agent should still answer. A free tier capped by an idle pause and an eight-hour run limit does not.

scenario.turn: Three trials end by starting a paid plan, the rest are spent. The cap that matters is not the credit but the idle pause and the continuous-runtime limit, because those decide whether the free machine can stay up.

questions: Is a card required, and does a paid plan start automatically when the trial ends?
Is the allowance money, hours or a machine — and at which size?
Can the free tier stay up, or is it capped by idle pause and session limits?
Is a second trial available on the same account or card?
What happens when the credit runs out: block, stop, or charge?
